fixes.explanation: Joshua is Moses' assistant (Numbers 11:28), so I get why he came to mind, friend. But the passage doesn't mention him in this scene. Aaron turns and speaks to Moses: “My lord, please do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.” The name that fits here is Moses.

Caleb, from the tribe of Judah (Numbers 13:6), isn't named in this scene, baker. Nobody else steps in here. Aaron's words go straight to Moses: “My lord, please do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.” So Moses is the answer.

Forty is a fair guess, friend. It's a number that shows up a lot in the Bible. But here the LORD says, “Let her be confined outside the camp for seven days…” Seven is the number in this verse, and after that she may be brought back in.

That's the one, baker. The text says Miriam and Aaron criticized Moses “…because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had taken a Cushite wife.” That's the reason the passage gives, so I'll leave it right there. Two siblings, one complaint, and it's about to go somewhere they didn't plan.

I wish it worked that way, friend. You know when you say something you figure nobody will ever hear, and then you find out it got around? Here, the text says plainly, “And the LORD heard this.” So it didn't stay between the two of them.

Right, friend. Moses cried out to the LORD, “O God, please heal her!” The one Miriam and Aaron criticized is the one who pleads for Miriam. I think that says a lot about Moses, and the text has just called him “a very humble man” (Numbers 12:3).
